message.content:
For \(k=1,2,\dots,p-2\), we have
\[
\frac{1}{k(k+1)}=\frac{1}{k}-\frac{1}{k+1}\pmod p.
\]
Therefore the given sum is
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{p-2} k^{-1}(k+1)^{-1}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{p-2}\left(k^{-1}-(k+1)^{-1}\right).
\]
This telescopes:
\[
=1^{-1}-(p-1)^{-1}.
\]
Since \(p-1\equiv -1\pmod p\), we get
\[
(p-1)^{-1}\equiv (-1)^{-1}\equiv -1\pmod p.
\]
Thus
\[
1^{-1}-(p-1)^{-1}\equiv 1-(-1)=2\pmod p.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{2}\).
